name: NA64 detector

placements.note: NA64 operates on the H4 beamline; CERN's Experimental Areas page confirms H4 is one of the beamlines located in EHN1, the hall this site record represents (owned by another workstream).

technology.value: Active beam-dump / missing-energy spectrometer: incoming electron tagged and tracked, its energy deposited in an electromagnetic calorimeter, with hermetic veto systems to catch any visible secondary particles so that missing energy signals an invisible decay

intervals.label: operating
intervals.quote: started operations at CERN's North Area in 2016

summary.plain: The NA64 detector tags and tracks incoming electrons, absorbs their energy in a calorimeter, and watches for cases where energy simply vanishes -- a possible sign of an invisible dark-sector particle.
summary.technical: Active beam-dump missing-energy spectrometer on the NA64 H4 beamline (EHN1), combining an electromagnetic calorimeter with hermetic veto detectors to reject visible final states.

notes: Placed at the existing site:cern-neutrino-platform-ehn1 (owned by another workstream); see experiment:na64 notes for the H4-in-EHN1 citation.
